title: Blue Owl’s Stack seeks a $5.9bn loan, feeding the AI data-centre debt boom
excerpt: Stack Infrastructure, the data-centre arm of the private-credit giant Blue Owl, is seeking a loan of about $5.9 billion, Bloomberg reported. content_html:
Stack Infrastructure, the data-centre arm of the private-credit giant Blue Owl, is seeking a loan of about $5.9 billion, Bloomberg reported.

The deal, if it closes, would rank among the larger single financings in a market that has become the engine room of the AI build-out.

Blue Owl has made itself central to that market. Through Stack and a string of joint ventures, it has become one of the biggest private financiers of the data centres AI needs, part of a wave of borrowing that now runs into the hundreds of billions.

The new loan follows quickly on the last. Stack raised $2.1 billion as recently as February, and the jump to nearly $6 billion in a matter of months is a measure of how fast the appetite for capacity, and for debt, is growing.

The structure is characteristic of the moment. Rather than fund data centres from cash, the companies building them increasingly borrow against the assets and the long-term contracts that anchor them, a model that spreads the enormous cost across lenders hungry for yield.

Blue Owl is no bystander in that shift. It has helped arrange tens of billions in financing for hyperscale projects, including large facilities tied to Meta, putting private credit where traditional banks have grown more cautious.

The scale is what has changed. Individual AI campuses now cost tens of billions to build, sums that outstrip what any single bank wants to lend, which has handed private-credit firms like Blue Owl a central role they did not hold a few years ago.

The caution has a reason. Data-centre debt is only as safe as the demand that underpins it, and a few high-profile wobbles, including a soured Oracle-linked deal, have reminded lenders that the AI boom carries real credit risk beneath the enthusiasm.

Oracle needed PIMCO to anchor a $16 billion financing after banks pulled back, and infrastructure funds from Blackstone to Brookfield are writing cheques that would have looked outlandish two years ago.

The lenders are betting on a simple proposition. Compute is scarce, the companies renting it are among the richest on earth, and the contracts behind these buildings can run for a decade, which makes the loans look, on paper, like some of the safest bets in infrastructure.

The risk is that the proposition is circular. Much of the demand comes from AI firms still burning cash, and some of the debt is being backstopped by chipmakers with their own reasons to keep the build-out going, which knits the industry’s fortunes tightly together.

Blue Owl’s size gives it room the banks lack. As a private-credit manager, it can hold loans that regulated lenders would balk at, and it has leaned into that advantage as the AI-infrastructure market has swollen.

The $5.9 billion figure, for now, is Bloomberg’s reporting rather than a closed deal. Terms, pricing, and the exact assets behind it will decide how the market receives it, and large data-centre loans have both sailed through and stumbled in recent months.

What is not in doubt is the direction. The money required to build AI has outgrown balance sheets and is being met, more and more, with borrowed capital, and Stack’s latest raise is another rung on a ladder the whole industry is climbing.

Each of these loans is a wager on the same future. If AI demand holds, the debt is cheap money against a durable asset; if it cools, the buildings and the borrowings will both look heavier than they do today.

For Blue Owl, the calculation is one it keeps making. The firm has decided that financing the picks and shovels of the AI rush is the safer way to profit from it, and a $5.9 billion loan is its latest move to stay at the front of that queue.

content_html_zh:
据彭博社报道，私人信贷巨头 Blue Owl 的数据中心部门 Stack Infrastructure 正在寻求约 59 亿美元的贷款。

该交易如果完成，将跻身于人工智能发展引擎市场的较大单笔融资之列。

蓝猫头鹰已成为该市场的中心。 通过 Stack 和一系列合资企业，它已成为数据中心人工智能需求的最大私人融资者之一，这是目前规模达数千亿美元的借贷浪潮的一部分。

新的贷款很快就跟在上一笔贷款之后。 Stack 在 2 月份筹集了 21 亿美元资金，几个月内就跃升至近 60 亿美元，这表明了人们对产能和债务的需求增长有多快。

该结构具有当下的特征。 建设数据中心的公司不再用现金为数据中心提供资金，而是越来越多地以资产和支撑数据中心的长期合同为抵押进行借贷，这种模式将巨大的成本分摊给渴望收益的贷方。

蓝猫头鹰并不是这一转变的旁观者。 它帮助为超大规模项目安排了数百亿美元的融资，其中包括与 Meta 相关的大型设施，使传统银行变得更加谨慎的私人信贷。

规模发生了变化。 目前，单个人工智能园区的建设成本高达数百亿美元，这一数字超出了任何一家银行的贷款意愿，这使得像 Blue Owl 这样的私人信贷公司占据了几年前所没有的核心地位。

这种谨慎是有原因的。 数据中心债务的安全性取决于支撑其的需求，而一些备受瞩目的波动，包括​​与甲骨文相关的交易的失败，已经提醒贷方，人工智能的繁荣在热情的背后带来了真正的信用风险。

在银行撤资后，甲骨文需要太平洋投资管理公司 (PIMCO) 提供 160 亿美元的融资，而从黑石 (Blackstone) 到布鲁克菲尔德 (Brookfield) 等基础设施基金正在开具两年前看起来很奇怪的支票。

贷款人押注于一个简单的提议。 计算资源稀缺，租赁计算资源的公司是世界上最富有的公司之一，而这些建筑背后的合同可以运行十年，这使得贷款在纸面上看起来像是基础设施领域最安全的赌注。

风险在于该命题是循环的。 大部分需求来自仍在烧钱的人工智能公司，而芯片制造商则以自己的理由支持了部分债务，以保持扩建的继续，这将行业的命运紧密地联系在一起。

蓝猫头鹰的体型给了银行所缺乏的空间。 作为一家私人信贷管理公司，它可以持有受监管的贷方不愿接受的贷款，随着人工智能基础设施市场的膨胀，它已经利用了这一优势。

目前，59 亿美元的数字只是彭博社的报道，而非已完成的交易。 条款、定价及其背后的确切资产将决定市场如何接受贷款，近几个月来，大型数据中心贷款既顺利又遭遇挫折。

毫无疑问的是方向。 构建人工智能所需的资金已经超出了资产负债表的规模，并且越来越多地通过借入资本来满足，而 Stack 的最新融资是整个行业正在攀登的阶梯上的又一个台阶。

每一笔贷款都是对同一个未来的赌注。 如果人工智能需求持续存在，那么相对于耐用资产来说，债务就是廉价资金；如果天气变冷，建筑物和借款都会看起来比今天更重。

对于蓝猫头鹰来说，它一直在进行计算。 该公司认为，为人工智能热潮中的锄头和铲子提供融资是从中获利的更安全方式，而 59 亿美元的贷款是其保持领先地位的最新举措。
